preamble:
Metal's simdgroup_matrix tables as pure functions of storage precisions and the numerics policy: the one combination resolver both Metal_backend mma hooks consult, the arm table it publishes (Backend_intf.codegen_capabilities.mma_arm), and the capability descriptor (Backend_intf.mma_capability) autotune seeds from.

They live here, outside the metal-gated Metal_backend, so they are tested wherever OCANNL builds, with no device (test/operations/mma_format_arm_tables, gh-ocannl-1246). The backend still gates the descriptor at the device level (Apple7 and later), which is why no arm names a floor.
content:
val bf16_accum_wide : unit -> bool

Whether bf16 reduction accumulators reside in f32 on this backend: under Numerics.Bf16_wide, and since gh-ocannl-2029 under Bf16_auto too -- only Bf16_narrow keeps the simdgroup_bfloat8x8 accumulator (whose intrinsic narrows once per 8-deep k block, unlike the per-step serial loop) and storage-width serial accumulators. The one predicate behind the backend's accum_prec and mma_accumulator, so emission and residency cannot disagree.

val mma_accumulator : d_prec:Ops.prec -> a_prec:Ops.prec -> b_prec:Ops.prec -> Ops.prec option

The precision a storage triple's accumulator fragment resides at, under the current numerics policy; None: no simdgroup_matrix form, the scalar fallback renders. Every fragment type follows from this precision, and the destination boundary converts exactly where it differs from the destination's storage precision.

val mma_arm : a_prec:Ops.prec -> b_prec:Ops.prec -> d_prec:Ops.prec -> scope:Backend_intf.mma_emission_scope -> Backend_intf.mma_arm option

mma_accumulator projected to an arm, the same in both emission scopes (gh-ocannl-1153): the backend's C_syntax.C_syntax_config.mma_arm.

val capability : Backend_intf.mma_capability

The tile-MMA descriptor of an Apple7+ device. Its mma_format_tiles lists the STORAGE triples mma_accumulator has an arm for; test/operations/mma_format_arm_tables checks the correspondence both ways under every numerics policy.

Operand loads (gh-ocannl-1456)

val tile : int

simdgroup_matrix's square extent: every arm's intrinsic tile is tile x tile x tile.

val k_loop_lines : a_frag:string -> b_frag:string -> acc:string -> ta:bool -> tb:bool -> lda:int -> ldb:int -> m:int -> n:int -> k:int -> string list

The reduction loop of an accepted m x n x k Tile_mma statement, as both of the backend's hooks render it: simdgroup_loads of the a and b tiles from __mma_ap / __mma_bp (with transpose_matrix for transposed storage, ta / tb) and simdgroup_multiply_accumulate into the mt x nt accumulator array acc. a_frag / b_frag are the operand fragment types.

val operand_fragments : a_prec:Ops.prec -> b_prec:Ops.prec -> d_prec:Ops.prec -> scope:Backend_intf.mma_emission_scope -> Backend_intf.mma_fragments option

How k_loop_lines brings the operands of a triple with an arm (mma_accumulator) into registers: the tile cube, each fragment once per reduction step, whole. The backend's C_syntax_config.mma_operand_fragments; test/operations/mma_format_arm_tables counts the loads k_loop_lines renders against it.

val operand_loads : a_prec:Ops.prec -> b_prec:Ops.prec -> d_prec:Ops.prec -> scope:Backend_intf.mma_emission_scope -> ta:bool -> tb:bool -> a:Backend_intf.mma_operand_place -> b:Backend_intf.mma_operand_place -> bool * bool

(false, false): Metal has no ldmatrix analogue — the hooks decline a swizzled operand, and every load k_loop_lines emits is a whole-fragment simdgroup_load. The backend's C_syntax_config.mma_operand_loads.
